item.title: VR on IPsec VPN Part 2 - Experimental Setup
item.description:
1. Introduction

In Part 1, we went through why IKEv2 is such a juicy (and painful) target. Before we can start crafting packets or poking at the state machine, we need a lab that we fully control.

We will be building strongSwan from source instead of pulling it from the package manager. There are two good reasons for this:

  1. Debug symbols – Compiling with -g -O0 makes life a lot easier when we start stepping through the daemon with gdb or cross-referencing functions in Ghidra later on.

item.title: VR on IPsec VPN Part 1 - First Peek Into The Rabbit Hole
item.description:
1. Introduction

This series is about vulnerability research against IPsec VPN, with IKEv2 as the main target. Before we start building labs or crafting packets, we need a clear picture of what IPsec actually gives us, why the attack surface is worth the pain, and how we plan to poke at it.

This first part stays high level on purpose. We will cover:

  1. What IPsec is and the properties it claims to provide.
  2. Why edge VPN implementations are such a juicy (and painful) target.
  3. How IKEv2 replaced IKEv1, and why that state machine is hard to fuzz.
  4. The lab and analysis approach we will use for the rest of the series.
